answer: Mains-hum fingerprints. Each seat plugs a $5 audio adapter into a wall outlet and streams the grid's 50/60 Hz wobble for a VRF-picked 10-minute window. Matching public grid-operator logs proves the trace is live; a replayed relic fails. Local harmonic noise differs per building, so keys whose residuals correlate above 0.95 merge into one seat. A farm needs a powered site per alias, about $30 a month of colo each: 1,000 sybils cost $30k a month. A cedar cabin on its own line passes; a key whose trace hops grids mid-window, a voyage no outlet makes, is flagged.
